objective: Break the tie between the two hard families. money-rollup ranks Python first and circuit-breaker ranks Python last, and each ordering follows from the affordance that family rewards. text-redact is a third family that rewards neither exact arithmetic nor union exhaustiveness: every offset and length in its contract counts Unicode code points, which Python indexes already, JavaScript and TypeScript do not, and Go forces into the open as string against []rune. If the three-family pattern is affordance-driven, the orderings should keep disagreeing and no arm should lead everywhere.

analysis.primary_estimand: per-family hidden-verifier pass rate by language, reported for all three families separately and never pooled into one score
analysis.uncertainty: Wilson intervals per arm within a family; paired bootstrap over attempt blocks for language contrasts
analysis.stopping_rule: Fixed at 120 rollouts, written down before the first paid call and before any result was looked at. No interim stopping and no continuation on observed pass rates. The v0.7 continuation was outcome-dependent and this design does not repeat it.

notes: configuration-merge is dropped from this cohort and text-redact takes its place. configuration-merge saturated at 100% correctness in v0.6 and again in v0.8, so it contributes to the effort outcomes only, and three families is the launch gate's minimum. money-rollup and circuit-breaker are carried forward unchanged so the new family is read against them within one cohort rather than across cohorts. Three families is still below the point where between-family variance is well estimated, so this supports claims about these three tasks and no language-general claim. text-redact has never been run against a model, so its difficulty is calibrated only in the sense that the gate is green and the starter fails ten of twelve; if it lands at the floor or the ceiling that is reported as a fact about the task, not repaired after the fact.

execution.note: Rollouts run four at a time. All three families are command-mode, so there are no HTTP servers, no port binding, and no timing-sensitive concurrency cases for contention to perturb; correctness, agent steps, and cost are unaffected. Wall-clock telemetry IS affected and is not reported as an outcome for this cohort. Batches are operational checkpoints for infrastructure health only. The stopping rule remains fixed at 120.
